annotation.summary_en: Full text of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (done at Vilnius, 5 September 2024), as published in the EU Official Journal in 2026. This first binding international AI treaty requires parties to make sure AI lifecycle activities respect human rights, democracy and the rule of law. It relies on principles, remedies, risk management and oversight mechanisms. It has no robot-specific provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Parties must adopt measures ensuring AI lifecycle activities respect human dignity, autonomy, equality, privacy, transparency, oversight and accountability
Graduated risk and impact management framework, including testing and assessment of the need for moratoria or bans
Accessible remedies, documentation for affected persons, and notification when interacting with AI systems
Each Party must set up independent oversight mechanisms; a Conference of the Parties provides follow-up
Applies to public authorities; private-sector coverage by declaration; national defence excluded
